# Two checkouts of one module share a vet result. A result that names a file
# names it by directory, so the second checkout must run the tool again and
# report its own file.

env GOCACHE=$WORK/gocache
mkdir $GOCACHE

cd first
go vet -json ./bad
stdout 'first.*bad\.go'
! stdout second

mkdir $WORK/second/bad
cp go.mod $WORK/second/go.mod
cp bad/bad.go $WORK/second/bad/bad.go
cd $WORK/second
go vet -json ./bad
stdout 'second.*bad\.go'
! stdout first

# The first checkout still reads its own result.
cd $WORK/gopath/src/first
go vet -json ./bad
stdout 'first.*bad\.go'
! stdout second

-- first/go.mod --
module m

go 1.20
-- first/bad/bad.go --
package bad

import "fmt"

// Print formats a string with the verb of a number.
func Print() {
	fmt.Printf("%d\n", "text")
}
